title: Design System: TonNam · ต้นน้ำ

display.purpose: Hero headlines on public surfaces only. Playfair Display. Forbidden on internal pages.

headline.purpose: Page-level H2 on public. Menu section headers.

title.purpose: H3 on public, major section titles on public.

body.purpose: All readable prose. Max 65–75ch. Noto Sans Thai on all surfaces.

label.purpose: Button text, form labels, nav items, badge text, internal primary text.

mono.purpose: ALL short IDs (B-0042, O-0117) and currency amounts in data tables. Never for body copy.

eyebrow.purpose: Section labels on public surfaces only, Terracotta color. Forbidden on internal pages.

shadows.name: subtle-lift
shadows.purpose: Small elements at hover, buttons at rest.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: Modals, drawers, command palettes, sticky headers when scrolled.

shadows.name: hero
shadows.purpose: Large focal elements on public pages. Green-tinted rather than brown.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus state on all interactive elements. Forest green tint.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Toggle switches, checkbox ticks, focus rings, hover background fills on internal.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: Card hover lifts, status badge color transitions, button press scale, dropdown open.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Page-level transitions, modal open/close, drawer slide, hero elements on public.

motion.name: ease-enter
motion.purpose: Enter animations. Elements arriving on screen.

motion.name: ease-trans
motion.purpose: State transitions. Elements changing in place.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Waiter App and Kitchen Display primary viewport.

narrative.overview:
TonNam is a Thai heritage restaurant. The design system runs on two parallel tracks: one for guests, one for staff. Neither track is a compromise of the other.

The Public Track (guest-facing: /, /menu) is full brand expression — deep forest green, warm gold accents, Playfair Display serif headings, generous cream backgrounds. It should feel like picking up a menu printed on cotton paper, or sitting in a dining room where the walls are made of something that took time.

The Internal Track (staff-facing: /pos, /waiter, /kitchen, /admin) is where the same brand becomes functional authority. Forest green returns as the primary action color. Noto Sans Thai carries everything. The palette steps down to a structured greyscale ink scale with forest green reserved for what matters: primary buttons, active navigation, key states. Staff should feel they are using a professional tool built specifically for TonNam — not a rebranded SaaS panel.

Both tracks reject the same failure modes: cold generic admin panels, loud gradient dashboards, sterile fintech neutrality, Western fine-dining minimalism that strips warmth in the name of whitespace.
keyCharacteristics: Two-track identity: warm heritage public / functional authority internal
Forest green (#1B4332) as the single brand anchor across both tracks
Warm brown-tinted shadows throughout — never neutral grey
Bilingual Thai + English on public; Thai-primary on internal
Monospace for all IDs and currency amounts (B-0042, ฿1,250.00)
Real-time state is always visible; the screen is always current

rules.name: The No-Pure-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Never use pure black (#000) or pure white (#FFF) as text or background on public surfaces. Dark Brown (#2C1810) and Warm Cream (#FAF6F0) are the floor and ceiling.

rules.name: The Gold Rarity Rule
rules.body: Gold (#C9A84C) appears on ≤15% of any given screen: italic emphasis in one heading word, prices, logo mark accent. Not as a background fill, not as decoration. Its scarcity is what makes it feel like value.

rules.name: The Track Rule
rules.body: The warm public palette (cream, brown, gold) and the greyscale internal palette (ink scale) do not mix within a single page. No Warm Cream on internal pages; no ink-50 on public pages. Forest green is the only color that crosses the line — and it does so deliberately.

rules.name: The Two-Font Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display is forbidden on internal pages (POS, Waiter, Kitchen, Admin). Noto Sans Thai handles all internal typography including headings. The serif is a guest-facing material, not a tool material.

rules.name: The Italic Gold Rule
rules.body: One italic-gold (#C9A84C) emphasis word per Playfair Display heading, maximum. Never two gold words in the same heading. Never italic-gold on body text.

rules.name: The Thai-First Rule
rules.body: All internal interfaces are Thai-primary. All IDs and currency values use monospace. Sentence case throughout — never ALL CAPS buttons.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this system is tinted with brand brown (rgba(44,24,16,...)) or brand green (rgba(27,67,50,...)). Never rgba(0,0,0,...). A neutral-grey shadow on any TonNam surface is a defect, not a design choice.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Internal pages are flat at rest. Shadows appear only on elevated surfaces (cards, dropdowns, modals) and as a response to interaction (hover lift, focused input ring). Depth on internal is earned through tonal background steps (ink-50 page → white card → ink-100 border), not shadow stacking.

dos: Do use Warm Cream (#FAF6F0) as the only page background on public surfaces. Never pure white on public.
Do use Dark Brown (#2C1810) for body text on public. Never pure black.
Do render all short IDs (B-0042, O-0117, T-05) and all currency amounts in JetBrains Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on currency columns.
Do write all Thai bill names and entity names verbatim (e.g. บิลโต๊ะ 5, โต๊ะ 3).
Do write button labels in sentence case, Thai-primary on internal (e.g. ยืนยันการชำระเงิน, Save changes).
Do reserve Playfair Display strictly for public surfaces: headings, hero text, the public CTA button, the logo.
Do tint all shadows with brand brown (rgba(44,24,16,...)) or brand green (rgba(27,67,50,...)).
Do animate WebSocket state changes — table status, order item cooked, payment confirmed — with 200ms ease transitions.
Do use text-wrap: balance on H1–H3 headings.
Do set touch targets to ≥44px on Waiter App and Kitchen Display.
Do include @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) for every animation.
donts: Don't use Playfair Display on any internal page (POS, Waiter, Kitchen, Admin). It is a guest-facing material, not a tool material.
Don't use the warm public palette (cream, gold, terra, brown) on internal pages. The Track Rule is absolute.
Don't use rgba(0,0,0,...) for shadows. Every shadow is warm-tinted. A neutral-grey shadow is a defect.
Don't reach for a modal as the default pattern for any task that could be done inline.
Don't use color as the sole state indicator. Every status badge carries a dot and a label.
Don't build the Kitchen Display like a web app. It reads like a physical ticket board: high contrast, large touch targets, no decorative elements.
Don't make internal staff tools look like rebranded SaaS panels (grey bodies, blue accents, Inter everywhere).
Don't build a Western fine-dining minimal public site. TonNam is Thai Heritage — warmth comes from color and material, not whitespace alone.
Don't use loud gradient dashboards with decorative chart animations on the Admin analytics views.
Don't use exclamation marks in any copy. The TonNam voice is quiet confidence.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient). Use a single solid color.
Don't use border-left colored accent stripes (>1px) on cards, callouts, or list items.
Don't hide WebSocket connection state from staff on any internal page.
